Documentation / Developer / Layer identity and compatibility boundaries

Layer identity and compatibility boundaries

MVR Layer UUIDs own persistent identity. Layer::name is authored presentation metadata; empty and equal names are valid in the repository's official MVR 1.6 schema. Imported layers are never coalesced or renamed to satisfy a GUI label policy. Canonical UUID spelling may normalize representation without replacing the effective UUID. The specification/XSD basis remains the pinned provenance in Architecture.

Fixture, Truss, Support, SceneObject, and GroupObject own layerUuid. Export, grouping, deletion, Query membership, visibility, and current-layer selection use UUIDs. Rename changes metadata and refreshes derived labels; it never changes object ownership. An authored foreign layer called No Layer is not special. Only the canonical application default UUID identifies the default layer, and only that identity is protected from user rename/deletion.

Core's GUI-independent layer_identity API owns UUID lookup, presentation labels, compatibility resolution, default creation, and migration. Empty names are presented as [<UUID>]; equal names get a full UUID suffix. These labels never overwrite Layer::name or enter standard MVR fields. User-created names still follow the separate LayerService UI policy: nonempty, bounded, and unique. Imported names are not subject to that policy.

Default and legacy migration

The application default is a normal Layer named No Layer, with UUID DeriveDeterministicUuid("mvr:layer:default"). Fresh project setup and production creation allocate canonical identities immediately. layer_default is accepted only as legacy input and maps deterministically to this default UUID. No production creation path emits that token or a layer_<timestamp> identity.

The shared MVR reader retains every Layer, even empty layers with empty names. It preserves valid UUIDs, repairs malformed/missing/conflicting source identities once in the parsed editable scene, and assigns children by the parsed Layer UUID. Source metadata used by Inspector remains separately recorded as authored. The legacy layer_default spelling uses the same canonical default policy.

MigrateLayerMembership is an explicit import/mutation compatibility boundary. For missing ownership, it prefers explicit child ownership, then unambiguous legacy label/name resolution. Absent legacy layers are inferred deterministically from their names. Ambiguous legacy assignments without child ownership are kept in a distinct inferred layer; migration does not guess between existing UUIDs. Repeated migration is idempotent. A nonempty authoritative ownership reference is never replaced by a name merely because the label disagrees.

Project and workspace state

.pstg persists scene identity through canonical scene.mvr, so the standard Layer/ChildList graph carries UUID ownership without a private MVR extension. Project restore uses the same reader and migration. view_hidden_layers now stores UUIDs; older name entries are resolved on load. A historical hidden name shared by several layers hides those same layers after migration. Current-layer selection is saved as view_current_layer_uuid; old projects lacking that key select the canonical application default. History snapshots include UUID state and object ownership, preserving Undo/Redo across rename and delete.

Remaining compatibility text

The old object layer string remains a derived label, because existing table widgets, natural sorting, and parts of GUI cache invalidation consume display text. Table adapters prepare label edits without mutating the scene, then commit UUID ownership after the Undo snapshot; creation adapters call AssignLayer. All persistent ownership decisions use layerUuid. Replacement/conversion paths copy UUID ownership independently. GetLayerNames remains a presentation API returning unique labels; UUID enumeration is separate and does not collapse names. Low-level LayerVisibilityState still accepts string tokens for old callers; ConfigManager resolves project/workspace inputs through the domain API before publication, and render/picking paths consume UUIDs. Legacy MVR appearance maps may resolve colors by name only when UUID-keyed appearance is unavailable; that fallback never chooses membership or changes identity.

Follow-up: replace the remaining table display strings with explicit UUID/value choices and compute labels at presentation time. This would remove the derived object label cache without changing the domain or standard serialization.

Defensive export boundary

RecoverSceneIdentities remains enabled. Export preparation and canonical snapshots operate on a private copy; read-only snapshots do not migrate or dirty the live scene. Import and legacy load store migration results in editable state, so normal export does not repeatedly repair application-generated identities. Malformed, missing, duplicate, conflicting, or unresolved identities introduced later still produce the established diagnostics. Representation normalization and source identity preservation remain separate concerns.
